MECH 220.title: Technical Skills Practicum
MECH 220.description: Engineering graphics, spatial visualization, CAD, equation solvers, machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting, elements of engineering science. .
MECH 220.prerequisiteText: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 100, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170 and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150

MECH 221.title: Engineering Science I
MECH 221.description: Rigid body kinetics and kinematics, basic electrical circuits, work and power, stress and strain, torsion, bending, engineering materials, probability and statistics. This course includes the content of ELEC_V 203.
MECH 221.prerequisiteText: All of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150

MECH 222.title: Engineering Science II
MECH 222.description: Fluid properties, equations of state. Pressure, buoyancy, hydrostatic forces. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. Work and heat; internal energy and enthalpy. Bernoulli's equation. Dimensional analysis, modelling. Turbulent flow in pipes; turbomachinery. Second law and the Carnot cycle; entropy; first and second law analysis of systems. .

MECH 223.title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process
MECH 223.description: Design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design projects representing both mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems. .

MECH 224.title: Integration of Engineering Concepts I
MECH 224.description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on dynamics, solid mechanics, materials, electronics, and mathematics. .

MECH 225.title: Integration of Engineering Concepts II
MECH 225.description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and mathematics. .

MECH 226.title: Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
MECH 226.description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design reports, business correspondence, verbal, online, and visual presentation of technical material. Restricted to students in the second year of Mechanical Engineering.
MECH 226.corequisiteText: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 221, MECH_V 222, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225

MECH 227.title: Approaches to Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
MECH 227.description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design, business correspondence, verbal, online and visual presentation of technical material. Focus on the linguistic structure and style of technical communication. Restricted to students in Mechanical Engineering. .
MECH 227.prerequisiteText: MECH_V 220 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150

MECH 230.title: Technical Skills Practicum I
MECH 230.description: Engineering graphics, spatial visualization, CAD, equation solvers, elements of engineering science. .
MECH 230.prerequisiteText: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of APSC_V 100, APSC_V 150, APSC_V 151; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150

MECH 231.title: Technical Skills Practicum II
MECH 231.description: Machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting.

MECH 232.title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process I
MECH 232.description: Introduction to design methodology, synthesis and analysis.
MECH 232.prerequisiteText: All of APSC_V 160, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 170; and one of APSC_V 100, APSC_V 150, APSC_V 151; and one of BMEG_V 102, PHYS_V 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL_V 112, WRDS_V 150

MECH 233.title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process II
MECH 233.description: Intermediate design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design project representing mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems.

MECH 260.title: Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
MECH 260.description: Statically determinate frames and trusses; normal and shear stresses and strains; shear force and bending moment diagrams; theory of beam bending, torsion of circular rods; transformation of stress and strain in two and three dimensions, Mohr's circle; yield and ultimate failure criteria. .
MECH 260.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of MATH_V 101, PHYS_V 170 or (b) all of APSC_O 172, APSC_O 173, APSC_O 180

MECH 280.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
MECH 280.description: Fluid properties; statics; kinematics, dynamics, energy, and momentum principles for control volumes; dimensional analysis and similarity; laminar and turbulent flow; pipe flow; principles of centrifugal pumps. .
MECH 280.prerequisiteText: All of MATH_V 152, PHYS_V 170 and one of MATH_V 217, MATH_V 253; and either (a) PHYS_V 131 and one of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118; or (b) PHYS_V 153 or (c) all of PHYS_V 157, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 159

MECH 305.title: Data Analysis and Mechanical Engineering Laboratories
MECH 305.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools.
MECH 305.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225

MECH 306.title: Data Analysis and Mechatronics Laboratories
MECH 306.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials and heat transfer. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. Common mechanical devices. For students in the Mechatronics Option only.
MECH 306.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225

MECH 325.title: Machine Design
MECH 325.description: Selection of flexible drives, bearings, fluid power system components, and couplings. Design of shafts, bolted joints and power screws. Design and selection of gears, gear trains, and mechanisms. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 360. .

MECH 327.title: Thermodynamics II
MECH 327.description: Air standard and vapor cycles; first and second law of cycles. Exergy. Gas mixtures. Energy conservation. Equilibrium. Reacting systems. Application to thermofluid systems such as power plants. .
MECH 327.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 328.title: Mechanical Engineering Design Project
MECH 328.description: Applying the design process, making educated assumptions and decisions, and working in teams to provide a new mechanical design. Weekly lecture discussing product development and various factors affecting the design. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher in Mechanical Engineering.

MECH 329.title: Materials for Mechanical Design
MECH 329.description: Selection of material properties for mechanical design. Metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites and other hybrid materials. .
MECH 329.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 224 or (b) all of APSC_V 278, MECH_V 260

MECH 358.title: Engineering Analysis
MECH 358.description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing emphasized. .

MECH 359.title: Computational Methods for Mechanical Engineering
MECH 359.description: Computational methods for solving mechanical engineering problems. Numerical computation of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations; interpolation and extrapolation; numerical integration and differentiation; numerical solution of differential equations.

MECH 360.title: Mechanics of Materials
MECH 360.description: Beam deflections, singularity functions; use of tabulated solutions; column buckling; Castigliano's theorem, statically indeterminate beams, bending of beams with asymmetric cross-sections, shear centre; principal stresses and stress invariants in three dimensions. .

MECH 366.title: Modelling of Mechatronic Systems
MECH 366.description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, thermal, fluid elements and mixed mechatronic systems. Signal processing, signal conditioning. Sensors, data acquisition systems, actuators.
MECH 366.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 223, MECH_V 224, MECH_V 225

MECH 368.title: Engineering Measurements and Instrumentation
MECH 368.description: Industrial measurement needs including: architecture of electronic instrumentation systems; electrical representation of physical quantities; sensors and actuators; analog signal processing using linear and non-linear circuits; computer-based readout including programming for user-interface and data acquisition.
MECH 368.prerequisiteText: Either (a) two of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 224, ELEC_V 203 or (b) all of MANU_V 230, ELEC_V 203

MECH 375.title: Heat Transfer
MECH 375.description: Steady and transient conduction. Radiation heat transfer. Convective heat and mass transfer in pipes and from external surfaces. Design of heat exchangers. .
MECH 375.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257, PHYS_V 203 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 380.title: Fluid Dynamics
MECH 380.description: Review of principles, compressible flow, potential flow, simple laminar viscous flow, boundary layers, flow around bluff bodies.
MECH 380.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of MATH_V 255 or MATH_V 256 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280 and one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257, PHYS_V 203

MECH 392.title: Manufacturing Processes
MECH 392.description: Manufacturing characteristics of materials and their control. Metal forming processes, plastic deformations, rolling, forging, drawing, extrusion, sheet metal forming. Machining processes and machine tools, turning, milling, drilling, grinding. Metal fabrication, welding and casting. An introduction to process planning. .

MECH 400.title: Professionalism and Ethics in Engineering
MECH 400.description: Professionalism, ethical frameworks, decolonization, equity, diversity, inclusion, law. Obligations of the engineer.

MECH 410.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
MECH 410.description: Lectures and readings on specialized topics of current interest in Mechanical Engineering.

MECH 411.title: Air Pollution, Technology and Society
MECH 411.description: Causes and effects of air pollution in the context of technology and society. Topics include: impact of air pollutants on air quality and climate, atmospheric science, public policy, collective action, environmental justice, science communication, economic externalities, and ethical engineering design. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. .

MECH 412.title: Engineering in Society and Technological Stewardship
MECH 412.description: Societal influences that affect engineering activities, including interactions between engineering and the economic, health, safety, legal, and cultural aspects of society; uncertainties in the prediction of such interactions; industrial policy; sustainable development; entrepreneurship; and environmental and technological stewardship.

MECH 420.title: Sensors and Actuators
MECH 420.description: Measurement of motion, stress, force, torque, temperature, flow and pressure; principles of sensors and signal conditioning methods; actuators.

MECH 421.title: Mechatronics System Instrumentation
MECH 421.description: Architecture of mechatronics devices; integration of mechanical, electronics, sensors, actuators, computer and real time software systems; PLC and PC based systems; discrete and continuous automation system design. .

MECH 422.title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
MECH 422.description: Fundamentals of MEMS (MicroElectroMechanical Systems). Microfabrication of MEMS with solid-state technology. LIGA and micro injection molding. Physics of MEMS. Operational principles of various MEMS devices. .
MECH 422.prerequisiteText: One of MECH_V 224, ELEC_V 204 and all of MECH_V 360, MECH_V 368

MECH 423.title: Mechatronic Product Design
MECH 423.description: Design of mechatronic systems for industrial and human-centric applications compliant structures; electronic circuits to interface with sensors and actuators; embedded systems; precision timing and control; data acquisition and processing; user interfaces; and product innovation.
MECH 423.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 366, ELEC_V 302, CPEN_V 312. and 4th year standing

MECH 426.title: Mechanical Design
MECH 426.description: Design of shafts and welded joints. Fatigue and fracture considerations in design: failure types, failure under static and dynamic loading, fatigue failure, crack initiation, and propagation. Introduction to the FEM in mechanical design. Students can only receive credit for one of MECH_V 326 or MECH_V 426.

MECH 430.title: Engineering Data Analysis
MECH 430.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. .

MECH 431.title: Engineering Economics
MECH 431.description: Discounted cash flows. Sources of funds, cost of capital. Effects of depreciation, taxes, inflation. Evaluation and comparison of economic models for engineering projects. Replacement decisions. Public project analysis. Risk analysis. Project control, inventory analysis, simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. .

MECH 433.title: Biofluids
MECH 433.description: Review of principles, Navier-Stokes equations, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in human body. .
MECH 433.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 435.title: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
MECH 435.description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Muscle and joint loads. Muscle mechanics. Musculoskeletal dynamics. Gait. Tissue mechanics of tendon, ligament, articular cartilage, and bone. Biomaterials. Application examples in orthopaedics including joint replacement and fracture fixation. Students who have received credit for BMEG_V 230 or 330 cannot also receive credit for MECH_V 435. .
MECH 435.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 221 or (b) all of APSC_V 278, MECH_V 260

MECH 436.title: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
MECH 436.description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, spine, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets. Recommended pre-requisites: MECH_V 224, or all of MECH_V 260 and BMEG_V 330. .

MECH 445.title: Fuel Cell Systems
MECH 445.description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion: fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Recommended prerequisites: MECH_V 327 and MECH_V 375.
MECH 445.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 453.title: Aerospace Capstone Design Project
MECH 453.description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and aerospace devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. .

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Aerospace Option

MECH 453.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 327, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360, MECH_V 426. And fourth-year standing in the Aerospace Option

MECH 454.title: Thermofluids Capstone Design Project
MECH 454.description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and thermofluids devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories.

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Thermofluids Option

MECH 454.prerequisiteText: All of MECH 325, MECH 327, MECH 328, MECH 360. and fourth-year standing in the Thermofluids Option

MECH 455.title: Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Capstone Design Project
MECH 455.description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical naval architecture and marine engineering devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. .

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Option

MECH 455.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360, MECH_V 380. And fourth-year standing in the Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Option

MECH 456.title: Energy and Environment Capstone Design Project
MECH 456.description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical energy and environment devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. .

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Energy and Environment Option

MECH 456.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 327, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360. and fourth-year standing in the Energy and Environment Option

MECH 457.title: Flex Capstone Design Project
MECH 457.description: A capstone design project designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories.
MECH 457.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in Mechanical Engineering

MECH 458.title: Mechatronics Capstone Design Project
MECH 458.description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and mechatronics devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories.

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Mechatronics Option

MECH 458.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in the Mechatronics Option

MECH 459.title: Biomechanics and Medical Devices Capstone Design Project
MECH 459.description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design and development of practical biomedical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. For students in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option only.

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option

MECH 459.prerequisiteText: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option

MECH 460.title: Advanced Mechanics of Materials
MECH 460.description: Mechanics of rubber, tissue, and gels at large viscoelastic deformation; large plastic deformations and damage of materials; mechanical characterization of materials (property extraction from mechanical tests); selected problems in linear elasticity.

MECH 462.title: Finite Element Analysis
MECH 462.description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametric elements. Development of computer programs for simple problems. Utilization of existing computer packages. Application to mechanical engineering problems. Recommended prerequisite: MECH 360.

MECH 463.title: Mechanical Vibrations
MECH 463.description: Theory of vibration of mechanical systems. Undamped 1 degree of freedom vibration, forced vibrations and resonance, damping, multiple degree of freedom systems, mode shapes and orthogonality, continuous systems, vibration measuring instruments and frequency spectrum analysis.

MECH 464.title: Industrial Robotics
MECH 464.description: Definition and classification of industrial robotic devices. Selection and implementation issues. Workcell environments. Forward and inverse kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning. Sensing and manipulation tasks. Control architectures. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 466 or MECH_V 467. .

MECH 466.title: Control Systems I
MECH 466.description: Introduction to control systems: system modelling and transfer functions; block diagrams; principles of feedback; stability; Bode plots; root locus methods; frequency response; control design. Laboratory experiments to support the lecture content.
MECH 466.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 224 or (b) MATH_V 255 and one of ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 202, ELEC_V 204, EECE_V 251, EECE_V 253; or (c) all of ELEC_V 204, ELEC_V 221, ENPH_V 270, MATH_V 255

MECH 467.title: Computer Control of Mechatronics Systems
MECH 467.description: Block diagrams and transfer functions, continuous and discrete domain transformations, feedback control system characteristics, control design in both continuous and discrete domain, absolute and relative stability, laboratory examples of Mechatronic systems design. Credit cannot be obtained for both MECH_V 466 and MECH_V 467.

MECH 468.title: Control Systems II
MECH 468.description: Introduction to state space control methods for linear systems including modal control, controllability, observability, linear quadratic regulators, optimal control. Recommended co-requisite: MECH_V 366.

MECH 469.title: Dynamic System Modelling
MECH 469.description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal systems; analytical models; model representations such as linear and bond graphs; response analysis; digital simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. .

MECH 470.title: Energy Conversion Systems
MECH 470.description: Energy supply and demand. Energy conversion chain. Electrical power generation using thermal power plants, renewable energy, and fuel cells. Rankine cycle steam power. Brayton cycle gas turbine power plants, intercooling, reheat, and regeneration. Internal combustion engines. Exhaust gas after treatment. Combined and binary cycles. Nuclear power. Recommended pre-requisites: All of MECH_V 327, MECH_V 375. .
MECH 470.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 471.title: An Introduction to Pulp and Papermaking
MECH 471.description: Overview of pulp and paper operations. Conversion of wood to fibre through mechanical or chemical pulping, processing of recycled fibre, the papermaking process and paper converting operations. Contemporary developments. .

MECH 473.title: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning
MECH 473.description: Principles of air conditioning; psychometrics and refrigeration. Heat transfer through building materials. Estimation of heating and cooling loads including the use of current software. System design. Ground, air and water source heat pumps. .

MECH 477.title: Aerospace Propulsion
MECH 477.description: Cycle analysis of jet engines, thermodynamic cycles, mechanics and thermodynamics of combustion, components and the performance characteristics of chemical rockets. The detailed analysis of operating characteristics of turbojet, turbofan, turboprop, afterburning, and ramjet propulsion systems. .

MECH 478.title: Internal Combustion Engines
MECH 478.description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power, and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Engine emission and control systems. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH_V 327. .
MECH 478.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MECH_V 225 or (b) one of CHBE_V 241, ENPH_V 257 and one of CHBE_V 251, CIVL_V 215, MECH_V 280

MECH 479.title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
MECH 479.description: Techniques for numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, including an introduction to the finite difference, finite volume and finite element approaches. Simulation of laminar and turbulent flows, including common turbulent models. Validation techniques. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH_V 380. .

MECH 481.title: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
MECH 481.description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow.

MECH 484.title: Aircraft Stability and Control
MECH 484.description: Basics of subsonic flight in the atmosphere; aircraft performance, stability and control, loading and air worthiness. Detailed example.

MECH 485.title: Aircraft Design: Structures
MECH 485.description: Structural components of aircraft, introduction to the finite element method, bending and buckling of thin plates. Design of aircraft wing and fuselage structures, moments of inertia for complex shapes. .

MECH 486.title: Introduction to Ship Design
MECH 486.description: This course introduces the ship design process from a Systems Engineering point of view. Topics include ship operational requirements, space and weight estimation, parametric design, optimization techniques, and the impacts of ship design on economics and the environment.

MECH 488.title: Introduction to Ship Hydrodynamics
MECH 488.description: Ship terminology, lines plans, ship hydrostatics, transverse and longitudinal stability of ships, dimensional analysis, ship resistance prediction; ship propulsion methods, propeller selection and design. Recommended prerequisites: One of MECH 380_V or CIVL 315_V, or enrollment in the NAME MEng or NAME MEL program.
MECH 488.prerequisiteText: One of MECH_V 225, MECH_V 280, or CIVL_V 215

MECH 489.title: Experimental Thermofluids
MECH 489.description: Experimental uncertainty. Design of experiments. Test facilities. Temperature and pressure measurement techniques and instrumentation. Velocity and flow rate measurement techniques. Flow visualization. Case studies of industrial and research experimental practice. .

MECH 490.title: Interdisciplinary CapstoneDesign Project
MECH 490.description: An extension to projects in the New Venture Design Program that introduces additional technical design principles and requirements. Registration for this program is only permitted for Mechanical Engineering students who are in the New Venture Design Program. Restricted to students with only fourth-year standing in Mechanical Engineering.

MECH 491.title: Computer-Aided Manufacturing
MECH 491.description: NC programming and machining with interactive CAD/CAM systems. Curve and surface geometry for tool-path generation. Tool-path generation methodologies. Geometric modelling techniques for simulation and verification of manufacturing processes. Introduction to Computer-Aided Process Planning. Supplementary tutorial laboratory experiments. Recommended co- requisites: MECH_V 392 or MANU_V 380.

MECH 493.title: Academic Research I
MECH 493.description: Research project directed by a faculty member in Mechanical Engineering. .

prerequisite.raw: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor

MECH 493.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor

MECH 494.title: Academic Research II
MECH 494.description: Additional research project directed by a faculty member in Mechanical Engineering.

MECH 495.title: Industrial Engineering
MECH 495.description: Organizational structure. Manufacturing systems and group technology. Classification and coding. Scheduling and sequencing of operations. Forecasting. Quality control for variables and attributes. Plant location. System reliability analysis. Advanced manufacturing automation concepts. .

MECH 496.title: Engineering Management
MECH 496.description: Organization structures. Management styles. Cost systems and control. Financial statements; accounting procedures. Budgets and performance control. Project management. Human resources management. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. .

MECH 497.title: Research Skills and Data Analysis
MECH 497.description: Research environment, funding and dissemination systems; literature reviews and critically evaluating papers; creating research questions; research ethics, data security and research records; equity, diversity, and inclusion in research. Recommended pre-requisite: Third-year standing. .

MECH 498.title: Research Communication
MECH 498.description: Scholarly writing and communication in engineering. Standard research genres such as journal articles, conference posters, and grant proposals. Students will write on the topic of their CREATE-U research. .

MECH 501.title: Thermodynamics
MECH 501.description: Thermodynamic principles, Maxwell relations, availability, irreversibility, and equilibrium. Introduction to statistical mechanics.

MECH 502.title: Fluid Mechanics
MECH 502.description: Governing equations; viscous incompressible flow, incompressible potential flow; incompressible boundary layers, stability and turbulence; compressible potential flow.

MECH 503.title: Linear Elasticity
MECH 503.description: Stress and strain in three dimensions, fundamental field equations of linear elasticity; equilibrium, compatibility, Hooke's law; Papkovitch-Neuber solution, plane stress and plane strain; torsion, torsion of thin-walled members with warping restraint; plate theory.

MECH 506.title: Linear Vibrations
MECH 506.description: Transient and steady state vibration analysis of continuous and discrete mechanical systems. Lagrange's equation and Hamilton's Principle. Measurement of vibration. Machinery health monitoring. Frequency domain analysis. Experimental modal analysis. Vibration of rotating machinery.

MECH 507.title: Analytical Dynamics
MECH 507.description: Newtonian mechanics; generalized co-ordinates and analytical mechanics; Lagrange equations; Hamilton's Principle; rotational motion and rigid body dynamics; Gyroscopic motion; phase space, equilibrium, and stability of motion; stability characteristics of autonomous systems; Hamilton-Jacobi method; applications.

MECH 509.title: Controls
MECH 509.description: State space model; stability; controlability; observability; Kalman decomposition; state feedback; observer; linear quadratic regulator; Kalman filter.

MECH 512.title: Experimental Methods in Mechanics
MECH 512.description: Operating principles of transducers for measuring typical quantities; the construction of transducers and factors controlling their measurement accuracy; electronic signal conditioning equipment and computerized data acquisition system.

MECH 514.title: Linear FEA in Solids and Heat Transfer
MECH 514.description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametic elements. Computer program development. Utilization of existing computer packages.

MECH 520.title: Control Sensors and Actuators
MECH 520.description: Review of control, instrumentation and design. Performance specification of control components, component matching, error analysis. Operating principles, analysis, modelling, design considerations of control sensors and actuators such as analog sensors for motion measurement, digital transducers, stepper motors, DC motors, induction motors, synchronous motors, and hydraulic actuators. Control techniques pertaining to actuators. Applications.

MECH 521.title: Fundamentals of Microelectromechanical Systems
MECH 521.description: Micro-fabrication of MEMS: solid-state technology and other micromachining techniques. Engineering principles of various MEMS devices.

MECH 526.title: Mechatronic System Design Project I
MECH 526.description: The design, analysis, manufacturability, instrumentation and computer control of a selected dynamic machinery assembly will be studied.

MECH 527.title: Mechatronic System Design Project II
MECH 527.description: The full assembly, instrumentation, computer and electronic interfacing, and testing of a dynamic machine.

MECH 529.title: Modelling of Dynamic Systems
MECH 529.description: Advanced modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, thermal and multi-domain systems; inter-domain analogies; analytical models in time and frequency domains; modelling tools; response analysis; digital simulation; practical project. Recommended pre-requisite: prior undergraduate coursework in dynamics, vibration, or electrical circuits.

MECH 533.title: Biofluids
MECH 533.description: Principles, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in the human body.

MECH 535.title: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
MECH 535.description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Static and dynamic analysis of the musculoskeletal system. Gait. Musculoskeletal tissue mechanics. Biomaterials. Advanced study of relevant problems in orthopaedics, including joint replacement, fracture fixation, and spinal disorders.

MECH 536.title: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
MECH 536.description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets.

MECH 540.title: Emerging Topics in Mechatronics, Manufacturing, Controls, and Automation

MECH 541.title: Computer Control of Multi-Axis Machines
MECH 541.description: Digital control laws for servo drives; state space and transfer function models of feed drives; tracking errors; trajectory generation of multi-axis machines; contouring analysis of multi-axes servo drives; real time linear and circular interpolation methods supported by laboratory applications.

MECH 542.title: CAD/CAM Principles and Practice
MECH 542.description: 3D geometric modelling; parametric representation of curves and surfaces; CNC machine tool programming; milling operations and setup; tool path generation for three- and five-axis sculptured surface machining.

MECH 544.title: Machine Tool Structures and Vibrations
MECH 544.description: Review of metal cutting mechanics, milling, static deformations of machine tools. Machine tool vibrations, forced and self-excited vibrations in machining, chatter, stability. Sensors for machine tool monitoring and adaptive control. Sensor assisted intelligent machining techniques.

MECH 559.title: Engineering Project Management Fundamentals
MECH 559.description: Students who have taken NAME_V 524 are not eligible to receive credit for this course.

MECH 562.title: Multivariable Feedback Control
MECH 562.description: Well-posedness and internal stability of feedback systems, performance limitations, uncertainty, LFT representations, robust stability and robust performance, model reduction, linear matrix inequalities, H- infinity control, multi-objective control, mu-analysis and synthesis, H-infinity gain- scheduling, control applications. Recommended prerequisite: MECH_V 466, MECH_V 468, ELEC_V 341 or equivalent.

MECH 563.title: Robotics: Kinematics, Dynamics and Control
MECH 563.description: Definitions and classification Kinematics: homogeneous transformations, manipulator kinematic equations, forward and inverse kinematic solution methods, differential kinematic equations, motion trajectories. Dynamics: Lagrange-Euler formulations, Newton-Euler formulation. Control: methods, robot control hierarchy, control of single joint and multiple link manipulators, advanced control methods.

MECH 570.title: Emerging Topics in Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, and Heat Transfer

MECH 572.title: Convection Heat Transfer
MECH 572.description: Governing equations for laminar and turbulent flow. Forced convection in internal and external flow. Free, and combined free and forced convection. Heat transfer at high velocities, in rarefied gases and in two-phase flow. Mass transfer.

MECH 576.title: Combustion
MECH 576.description: Thermodynamics of combustion, stoichiometry, heat of formation and reaction. Equilibrium composition and adiabatic flame temperature. Chemical kinetics of combustion. Flames in premixed gases; laminar and turbulent flame propagation. Diffusion flames, pollutant emissions and combustion in IC engines.

MECH 577.title: Fuel Cell Systems
MECH 577.description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion; fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution.

MECH 578.title: Internal Combustion Engines
MECH 578.description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Numerical engine modelling and analysis.

MECH 581.title: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
MECH 581.description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow.

MECH 582.title: Experimental Fluid Mechanics
MECH 582.description: Modelling Test facilities. Wind tunnel force measurement. Theory of conventional and modern manometry. Classical velocimetry. Hotwire anemometry. Theory and application of laser Doppler velocimetry. Particle image velocimetry. Flow visualization techniques. Thermometry.

MECH 586.title: Turbulent Shear Flow
MECH 586.description: The basic equations of fluid motion; introduction to hydro-dynamic stability; Reynolds' equations; energy equations for turbulent motion; intermittency; similarity near a solid boundary and in free turbulence; approximate methods for predicting the growth of turbulent boundary layers and free symmetrical shear flows.

MECH 587.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
MECH 587.description: Analytical, computational, and experimental methods in fluid mechanics. Overview of CFD program development. Finite volume methods, spacial discretization and spatial accuracy analysis. Boundary conditions. Time advance methods, time accuracy, and stability. Application to model problems and to the incompressible laminar Navier-Stokes equations. Validation techniques for CFD codes.

MECH 588.title: Advanced Topics in Computational Fluid Dynamics
MECH 588.description: Selected advanced topics in CFD, typically chosen from: Finite volume methods on curvilinear meshes and structured mesh generation. Finite volume methods on unstructured meshes. Multigrid methods for elliptic PDE's. Reynolds-averaged form of the Navier-Stokes equations and turbulence modelling. Three-dimensional flows. Compressible flows.

MECH 590.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
MECH 590.description: Special advanced lecture courses may be arranged for graduate students upon the approval of the department head. There will not be more than 6 credits in any one such course.

MECH 597.title: Project for M.Eng. Studies
MECH 597.description: Project on assigned topic of specialization. For students registered in the M.Eng. program whose project is supervised by a faculty member in the department of Mechanical Engineering.

MECH 598.title: Research Seminar
MECH 598.description: Current topics in mechanical engineering research for M.A.Sc. students. Pass/Fail.

MECH 698.title: Seminar
MECH 698.description: Current topics in mechanical engineering for doctoral students. Pass/Fail.
